# Implementation status

## Explicit Memo/OLE storage checks

The default engine now exposes a separate bounded
[`check_table_long_values` service](access/storage/LONG_VALUE_CHECKS.md). It checks
qualified ACE 16 column maps, allocated LVAL pages and complete live descriptors,
and reports orphan storage and sharing without treating them as corruption or
write authority. Unknown, historical, indirect-candidate and unsupported profiles
remain explicit. Ordinary Memo/OLE reads keep their existing behavior.

The [scoped record](testing/results/long-value-storage-native-2026-10-26.json)
records 148 distinct passing runtime functions and three compile-fail checks.
Two frozen read-only consumers each checked the same 60 saved independent-writer
outputs, with all 120 column reports matching independently captured expectations.
These are storage-check results, not new UPDATE actions or native Access
qualification. General Memo/OLE replacement and normal ACE saves remain unfinished.

## Mixed indirect long-value map support

The default storage checker and existing engineering replacement API now admit
qualified indirect-owned/inline-candidate column maps through the same strict
represented-map grammar. Complete storage checks include bitmap allocation,
owned/candidate membership and live descriptors. Replacement retains immutable
request/map authority, existing represented EOF cells and independent final replay.
No new map, bitmap pointer or candidate window is created.

The [scoped record](testing/results/ace16-indirect-lval-native-2026-10-27.json)
passes 112 distinct runtime functions, including twelve new functions, plus three
compile-fail doc tests, strict/default lint, minimal compilation, rustdoc and
formatting. A separate working default checker returns all four exact expected
column reports on the two unchanged new originals. That diagnostic is read-only,
not a candidate replay or a committed-consumer qualification.

An initial independent fixture had an invalid bitmap signature and was corrected
without relaxing the four-byte parser grammar. A previously unsupported-map test
now correctly rejects its globally free bitmap. Initial failures remain recorded.
The [first committed-consumer original-file replay](testing/MIXED_LONG_VALUE_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now passes twelve exact images and fresh getter/map inspections on unchanged
sources. All twenty-five fixture commands succeed, including explicit NULL and
forwarded-parent cases. Indirect candidate maps, map/pointer growth, arbitrary
free-page reuse, reclamation and normal saves remain open.

## Indirect long-value map source observations

A separate [public-builder source phase](testing/INDIRECT_LONG_VALUE_MAP_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now captures two unchanged ACE 16 originals with indirect Memo owned maps and
inline candidate maps. All thirteen first-attempt construction/getter commands
pass. Each original has 702 user rows; 700 padding pages separate the two Memo
chains, giving a 716-page owned span. Both use one existing owned bitmap; candidate
windows shift and remain inline. No map bits, field flags or headers were patched.

A saved read-only verifier rebuilds all six checkpoints and compares complete
record bodies, live chunks, map roles and prospective mutable-map storage claims.
These observations do not expand engine admission or qualify indirect candidate
maps, map growth, replacement candidates or native Access saves. The default
storage checker and engineering preview retain their documented restrictions.

## Memo/OLE map edit authority correction

The engineering preview now proves exclusive map identity and storage authority
before changing membership, including empty maps. An adversarial literal fixture
previously let one table acquire another table's new LVAL page through shared
empty map rows. The [correction](testing/LONG_VALUE_MAP_AUTHORITY.md) rejects that
case and independently repeats the census against the immutable original during
final certification. Distinct map rows sharing a container remain supported.

The scoped batch passes 85 distinct runtime functions, including eight new
functions, plus three compile-fail doc tests and strict/minimal checks. Separate
read-only diagnostics admit both Memo columns on all 22 unchanged original-source
files (44 probes); they do not stage, finalize or publish candidates. Earlier
frozen-consumer acceptance remains historical evidence, not a replay of this
correction. Indirect candidate maps and normal native saves remain unfinished.

## Ordinary Memo/OLE replacement candidates

The separate `preview_ace16_long_value_updates` engineering API now replaces
qualified Memo/opaque OLE values through NULL, inline, single and chained
storage. Column-specific append/EOF allocation and ordinary parent forwarding
share one map ledger. Old chunks and orphan storage remain unchanged and allocated.

An immutable original operation supplies final row/value authority; independent
map, page and payload audits protect the actual candidate. Cross-catalog ownership
must qualify, including historical declarations and live references without map
pairs. Unknown ownership, sharing, unqualified extended fields, selected properties
and indexes remain explicit blockers. See the
[storage contract](testing/ACE16_LONG_VALUE_UPDATES.md).

The [scoped record](testing/results/ace16-long-value-updates-native-2026-10-27.json)
passes 99 distinct core runtime functions, three compile-fail checks, strict lint,
minimal compilation and formatting. A separate engineering consumer supports
quoted TSV requests with an explicit larger value profile, with fourteen distinct
consumer tests recorded separately. Original-file candidate qualification requires a frozen committed
consumer; the prior public transition corpus is not candidate evidence.
The first frozen 60-case original-file attempt refused all cases atomically,
without output: V2016 returned unsupported-column errors and V2019 returned
malformed-structure errors. Selected field metadata matches the intended raw
profile. The [preserved refusal record](testing/LONG_VALUE_UPDATE_REFUSALS.md)
separates that outcome from the subsequent diagnosis: the census rejected a
known opaque system backing field and interpreted a valid empty deleted slot
before checking its flags. The [correction](testing/results/ace16-long-value-census-correction-2026-10-27.json)
passes 152 distinct runtime functions and three compile-fail checks; both complete
original catalog censuses now pass read-only. The separate
[revised-artifact acceptance](testing/LONG_VALUE_UPDATE_ACCEPTANCE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now matches all 60 unchanged controls through the committed corrected consumer:
60 complete expected images and 120 read-only getter/map captures pass. Eight
NULL, 28 inline, twelve single and twelve chained values retain original chunks
and sibling/index identities; twelve parent records forward to new hidden rows.
The original zero-of-60 failure remains a separate immutable result. This does
not qualify compressed/extended fields, normal saves or native Access behavior.

Multiple represented candidate hints now use an explicit highest-first engineering
policy for LVAL chunks and ordinary parent forwarding. Each real failed fit clears
only its hint, lower hints are tried before EOF allocation, and the independent
map audit derives every attempt from original capacity. The
[focused record](testing/results/ace16-long-value-multiple-candidates-2026-10-27.json)
passes 34 distinct runtime functions, including six new controls for complete
images, slot ceilings, no-ops, unowned hints and correlated attempt/map forgeries.
Original-file multiple-hint behavior remains unqualified.

Exact ordinary Memo type 12, flag 2, extended flag 1 now has the same storage
checks and engineering replacement path. The writer emits compact narrow bytes
only for three through 1,024 eligible UTF-16 units; NUL/wide/supplementary or longer
text stays raw. Exact decoder roundtrip rejects leading-FEFF ambiguity instead
of silently changing requested text. A separate request-derived payload verifier
checks mode and every byte without calling the encoder. OLE ext1 and unknown
extended shapes remain refused. The
[compressed implementation record](testing/results/ace16-compressed-memo-native-2026-10-27.json)
passes 68 distinct runtime functions, including eight new functions, three
compile-fail checks, scoped feature/default strict checks, minimal compilation
and formatting. Its [first original-file candidate replay](testing/COMPRESSED_MEMO_ACCEPTANCE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now matches all 148 frozen controls: 132 exact complete images/getter results and
sixteen typed atomic refusals for lossy leading-FEFF requests. The source strings,
metadata, selectors and budgets are unchanged; no public writer action is rerun.
The sixteen refusals are distinct from the public writer's normalization results.
No semantic no-op or multiple-hint selection is qualified by this corpus.

## Compressed Memo reference observations

Two [finite public-writer experiments](testing/COMPRESSED_MEMO_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
complete 148 updates in 456 bounded processes. Of those, 132 requested values
reopen exactly and sixteen leading-FEFF inputs normalize; those sixteen are
explicit observations, not value-equality passes. Exact encoded streams establish
this writer's compression boundary at 1,024 UTF-16 units, together with its
minimum length and narrow-unit restrictions. Mixed/NUL and longer values stay
raw. No production encoder or native Access qualification follows automatically.

Read-only verification rehashes both saved reports and confirms 1,302 cumulative
old-chunk comparisons, 1,332 stable map-wire proofs and 140 direct decoder streams.
The tracked Java helper is byte-identical to the executed source; later Python
capture wrappers are explicitly separate. Raw Memo/OLE candidate acceptance and
its unchanged inputs remain independent of these observations.

## Fixed Int32 recursive split candidates

The separate feature-gated `preview_ace16_split_int32_updates` service can turn a
qualified overflowing single-Int32 root leaf into a height-one root and two EOF
leaves. It preserves logical row references, complete key/row bounds, unrelated
index bytes and counters, and updates only represented index-owned/global map
cells. Other-codec overflows still refuse. Existing fixed, page and
variable previews retain their previous admission and behavior.

The [split contract](testing/ACE16_INDEX_SPLITS.md) describes request-derived row
authority, independent page/map audits and non-journalable output. Scoped checks
pass 173 distinct runtime functions, including 153 existing regressions, and three
compile-fail checks. Strict lint, standalone minimal compilation and rustdoc pass.
The subsequent [two original-file candidates](testing/ROOT_SPLIT_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
both pass on their first run through a frozen committed consumer. Each complete
image matches the independently frozen model, including all 500 row references,
250/250 leaf partitions, map changes and preserved unrelated index bytes.
Native Access, data-macro semantics and normal saves remain unqualified.

The service now also splits existing non-root leaves when every resulting parent
fits. A new left leaf precedes the retained right page; neighbor links and full
key/row parent bounds are repaired without changing the root ID or height.
The [non-root scoped record](testing/results/ace16-nonroot-index-splits-native-2026-10-27.json)
passes 100 distinct runtime functions, including retained root-leaf regressions,
and three compile-fail checks. That stage refused internal-node overflow.
The [two original-file candidates](testing/NONROOT_SPLIT_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now pass on their first run, with complete independent image proofs. Each adds
one EOF leaf while preserving original Memo/OLE descriptors and chunk pages.

The [non-root reference capture](testing/NONROOT_INDEX_SPLIT_OBSERVATIONS.md)
records two current-service refusals and two successful public updates. Its first
verifier's exit 1 is retained: the reference writer also reallocated unchanged
Memo/OLE values. Read-only diagnosis verifies their equal payloads and the actual
new-left/retained-right leaf split. These are the preceding frozen consumer's
results, not successful non-root TableCraft candidates.

The subsequent recursive implementation now propagates full child maxima through
internal-parent splits. Non-root splits insert a new left sibling and retain the
original right page; root growth retains the root ID and adds right/left internal
pages beneath two bounded maxima. All sibling levels are rebuilt from final
child order, original unused bytes remain intact and fresh unused bytes are zero.
The independent auditor replays original counts, capacities, EOF allocation,
framing and maps without trusting the builder's arena. The
[new scoped record](testing/results/ace16-parent-index-splits-native-2026-10-27.json)
passes 108 distinct runtime functions, including eight new controls, and three
compile-fail checks, plus strict lint, minimal compilation, rustdoc and formatting.
The [four original-file candidates](testing/RECURSIVE_INDEX_SPLIT_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now pass on their first run through a frozen committed consumer: both retained-root
growth images and both below-root internal splits match the independent complete
images, fresh getters, row identities and maps. Their eight native/JVM fixture
commands remain separate from the reference writer actions. Normal saves,
other-codec splits and native Access qualification remain unfinished.

## Index-owned map promotion

The optional engineering split services now support
[same-extent inline index-owned map promotion](testing/ACE16_INDEX_MAP_GROWTH.md).
The existing map record becomes indirect when the complete required member span
cannot fit an inline window. A separate EOF usage bitmap stores original members
and actual new index pages; the bitmap is globally allocated without becoming
an index member. Recursive/repeated allocation shares this planner and independent
replay. No normal save or journalable edit path is added.

Independent complete-image controls cover two physical owners and real logical
aliases, shared global bytes, promotion after an earlier represented reservation,
and a mixed promoted/represented peer. Promotion operations require original
catalog exclusivity for every affected reserved owner, not just promoted maps.
Earlier inline cell edits are absorbed into the new bitmap rather than applied
to the rewritten pointer row. Every appended index/usage page is independently
classified and checked; this prevents ordinary/LVAL target activation, without
claiming global foreign-payload health or identical malformed-input errors.

The scoped batch passes 92 distinct runtime functions, including fifteen new
functions, plus three compile-fail checks, strict/default lint, minimal builds,
rustdoc and formatting. One old unsupported-width regression exposed a changed
handler error order; recognizing the supported shape before census restored the
original refusal without changing its test or fixture.

The [first committed-consumer replay](testing/INDEX_MAP_GROWTH_UPDATE_OBSERVATIONS.md)
now passes both unchanged public originals. All four native/getter commands
succeed, and each candidate matches its pre-execution whole-image expectation,
including exact pointer/global bytes, protected source residue and fresh padding.
Both source files and all reviewed input pins remain unchanged. Candidate/ordinary
map growth, shifted-inline windows, new map containers, global bootstrap, free-page
reuse, reclamation and native Access saves remain unfinished.

## Shared native map authority

The engineering [map-authority service](testing/ACE16_MAP_AUTHORITY.md) now
captures canonical map owners across the complete local catalog, including
ordinary, physical-index and current/historical long-value maps. Operations select
explicit mutable owners; exact record ranges and bitmap/container footprints
must be exclusive. Logical aliases of one physical index remain one owner, and
disjoint map rows may share their container. This is footprint authority, not
payload membership, writable-cell authority or implemented map growth.

The existing Memo/OLE replacement service consumes this shared inventory while
retaining its five selected owners, separate payload/live-reference checks and
immutable-original final recensus. Unreferenced physical index slots now refuse
write authority explicitly even when ordinary reads and LVAL storage checks pass.
The scoped batch passes 43 distinct runtime functions, including five new
functions, plus three compile-fail checks and scoped strict/default lint, minimal
compilation and formatting. All 44 separate source admissions pass on 22 unchanged
originals; these are not mutation candidates. Per-table read-count ceilings remain
separate from the shared operation budget. Check ordering and paid work need not
match the previous implementation exactly.

A [separate independent-writer experiment](testing/USAGE_MAP_GROWTH_OBSERVATIONS.md)

The eighteen recorded fixture commands comprise thirteen source successes, one

earlier exact-span corpus and Microsoft Access qualification.

## Bounded original-row request matching

The shared mutation walker now uses a paid original-position directory for
multiple requests, retaining full physical traversal and exact callback order.
Ordered captures skip sorting; empty/single requests avoid directory allocation.
Six private controls and 150 existing update/delete functions pass, and both
isolated builds reproduce sixteen accepted original-file candidate images.
The [balanced Hyperfine record](testing/ROW_REQUEST_DIRECTORY_OBSERVATIONS.md)
retains every sample: 500-row end-to-end timings are mixed/tied, so no uniform
speedup is claimed. Finite 16,384-request work bounds are established separately;
upfront allocation can change insufficient-resource error precedence.

## Typed multivalue parent joins

Explicit collection-aware retrieval now transports whole stored lists through
INNER joins and comma-separated CROSS sources, including nested joins and static
named/derived leaves. Scalar ON conditions select parent pairs before hidden
member WHERE criteria; selected lists retain their complete contents. Scalar-only
leaves keep their ordinary read service. Typed outer joins now use the explicit
absence model described above; whole-list UNION retains its explicit refusal,
while mixed list/displayed-member output now uses the expansion service above.
Scalar member aggregates use the existing
`.Value` query path.

The selected query batch passes 242 tests, including sixteen new controls, with
strict query lint and a standalone minimal build. Four isolated depth tests pass
on a 1 MiB stack. A newly exposed preparation overflow was fixed by separating
recursive join traversal from post-child construction; plain fifty-level named
queries retain their existing support. See the [query contract](query/collections/MULTIVALUE_QUERIES.md)
and [scoped verification](testing/results/read-query-typed-multivalue-joins-2026-10-26.json).
These checks do not establish native Microsoft Access query equivalence or finish
the read/query roadmap.

Eight native-adapter and three CLI integration tests pass, with selected strict
lint. The frozen committed CLI also matches 72 controls over three unchanged
native databases and their registered getter transcripts: 198 successful rows,
780 cells and 24 expected errors/refusals. See [host verification](testing/results/typed-multivalue-join-host-2026-10-26.json)
and the [independent parent-pair replay](testing/TYPED_MULTIVALUE_JOINS.md).

## Typed multivalue query results

The explicit collection-aware query API returns complete stored lists alongside
scalar expression values. Lists preserve order, duplicates, NULL members, empty
membership and stored IEEE representations without becoming core scalar values
or implicitly entering arithmetic. Ordinary scalar and `.Value` paths retain
their existing finite-value and publication rules.

CLI `query run --database PATH --multivalues` and `--collections` now display bare
list fields, including aliases, static named/derived projections, scalar
filtering/order/TOP and direct hidden `.Value` membership criteria. Typed list
INNER/CROSS and LEFT/RIGHT joins now use the separate service described above;
UNION, list keys and aggregates remain unsupported. Buffered schema
discovery retains its existing authorized scalar dependency reads before final
typed admission; collection scans require successful admission.

See [the query contract](query/collections/MULTIVALUE_QUERIES.md),
[CLI presentation](access/queries/NATIVE_QUERIES.md#explicit-multivalue-queries),
[query verification](testing/results/read-query-multivalue-results-2026-10-25.json),
[native adapter verification](testing/results/bare-multivalue-native-conformance-2026-10-25.json)
and [CLI verification](testing/results/read-query-multivalue-cli-2026-10-25.json).
These bounded services do not complete the read/query roadmap or establish
native Microsoft Access display, ordering or query equivalence.

## Reverse-search callback bounds

Reverse substring searches now reject provider spans that would publish a
position beyond the requested start, including an empty span at the exclusive
boundary. Decoded and retained UTF-16 callbacks share this validation. Existing
interior and forward empty spans retain their explicit provider contract.

Five new tests and 35 selected search regressions pass, with strict lint,
formatting and a standalone minimal build. A before-fix probe records three real
failures. See [the search contract](expressions/text/STRING_SEARCH.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-reverse-search-bounds-2026-10-25.json).
This fixes callback validation without qualifying native locale behavior.

## LIKE pattern error timing

LIKE now defers malformed-pattern errors until matching reaches the affected
element. Earlier mismatches return FALSE; a reached star validates suffix grammar,
while range ordering invokes the comparison provider only at a reachable class.
Both ANSI modes, scalar and retained UTF-16 paths share this explicit formal
profile. Empty-input behavior is documented separately from native ACE evidence.

Ten new tests and 209 selected regressions pass across matcher, evaluator, query
and CLI layers, with strict lint, formatting and standalone minimal checks. Eager
operand errors, NULL handling and cumulative resource limits remain explicit. See
[pattern error timing](expressions/text/PATTERN_MATCHING.md#pattern-error-timing) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-like-timing-2026-10-25.json).

Native consistency checks now cover all already-qualified ignore-NULL key
profiles, including composite keys. Independent sequential counts omit only
roots whose entire key is NULL; partially NULL keys remain eligible, and required
keys still reject any NULL component. Physical membership does not establish a
complete-table index scan or write eligibility.

Fifteen new tests and 198 selected regressions pass, along with strict lint and
minimal-feature checks. Complete-table constructors, public seek limits and
mutation gates retain their existing boundaries. See
[the check contract](access/NATIVE_CHECKS.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-ignored-index-coverage-2026-10-25.json).

existing contracts.

named/crosstab/progressive execution, checked limits, cancellation and plan reuse.

[the category contract](expressions/numeric/DECLARED_ARITHMETIC.md#null-literal-provenance) and

Thirteen new tests and 196 selected regressions pass across expression, matcher,

## Progressive fixed-key DISTINCT

Explicit streaming now admits terminal DISTINCT over proven Boolean, integral,
Currency, Decimal and NULL output tuples. It retains first encountered values,
finishes all input and eager checks before publishing distinct rows, and applies
TOP afterward. An arm's DISTINCT runs before outer UNION ALL conversion. Existing
exact key directories and cumulative budgets govern retained results; no complete
source snapshot or unsupported fallback is introduced.

Twelve new query tests, three new CLI tests and 266 selected regressions pass
across the complete progressive lifecycle batch and CLI streaming target.
Focused strict lint and repository formatting pass; independent review found no
blocker. See [the contract](cli/STREAMING_QUERIES.md) and

Text/float/date/GUID/Binary/Dynamic output profiles, inner DISTINCT and DISTINCTROW
remain outside this progressive profile. Buffered execution retains its own scope.

and [scoped verification](testing/results/encryption-page-copies-2026-10-25.json).

## Explicit inspection work allowance

`inspect --native-steps` now accepts an explicit cumulative work allowance under
the existing 100,000,000-step cap. Defaults and independent byte/row limits remain
unchanged. This lets callers budget full long-payload/index checks without changing
which profiles qualify. Sixteen CLI checks pass, including one new control for
work exhaustion, independent byte exhaustion, range rejection, unchanged complete
output and original bytes. Strict CLI linting and formatting pass. See the
[verification record](testing/results/inspect-native-work-2026-10-25.json).

## Progressive aggregate lifecycle extraction

The existing global, exact-key, Text and HAVING streaming consumers now share
concrete initialization, retained-row input and completion services. Intermediate
completion preserves raw Strings, natural value carriers and unknown declarations;
only the terminal wrapper applies scalar publication and UNION conversion. Typed
receiver failures stop later final expressions. This refactor does not enable
inner stateful queries; their admission remains refused pending the stage driver.
Two new receiver controls and 632 existing query/native/CLI regressions pass,
with strict query/host linting, minimal query features and formatting.
An initial host build exhausted disk before tests; the identical command passed
after removing old generated incremental caches. See the
[scoped verification record](testing/results/read-query-progressive-lifecycle-2026-10-25.json).

## Progressive Text grouping

Proven Text key tuples now wait for checked EOF and complete comparison-policy
cohorts before strict SQL partitioning. First values and raw String ranges remain
intact. Count/key-only selections retain keys without source-row replay frames;
operand-bearing groups use budgeted rows, with HAVING still suppressing rejected
SELECT work. Key storage can grow with the input, and many distinct Text groups
can require quadratic comparison work. Twenty-seven new controls and 605
regressions pass, including the original example under stored database policies
with snapshot ceiling one. Strict query/native/CLI linting, minimal query features
and formatting pass. See [phases and limits](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-text-groups-2026-10-25.json).
The [original native/CAB replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_TEXT_GROUPS.md) passes all
96 commands, comparing 1,272 successful rows/4,296 cells plus six exact earlier
error-prefix rows. Six rich Ordinal controls use an explicit work allowance after
default-work refusals; SQL and expected results are unchanged. Fifteen immutable
and forty-five revision-source hashes were independently rechecked. Native Access
grouping and mixed-policy qualification remain separate.

## Exact Currency and Decimal relational directories

Uniform Currency/Decimal GROUP BY, DISTINCT, qualified DISTINCTROW and UNION
keys now use bounded candidate directories with the existing SQL comparer as the
answer authority. Decimal fingerprints normalize a local coefficient/scale view;
retained representatives keep their original values, scale and policy lineage.
Active paired metadata also admits these keys in progressive grouping/HAVING.
Mixed carriers retain the original path. Twelve-thousand-row fixed-key controls
fit finite work allowances. Twenty-four new controls and 427 regressions pass,
with strict query/native/CLI linting, minimal query features and formatting.
See [proof and fallback](query/keys/EXACT_QUERY_KEYS.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-exact-fixed-keys-2026-10-25.json).
The [original native/CAB replay](testing/EXACT_FIXED_KEYS.md) passes 90 controls,
including 84 new-query successes comparing 14,088 rows and 41,802 cells. The old
1,100-key Decimal grouping needs increased work; the new path fits default work.
Sixteen immutable and seventy-one revision-source hashes were independently
checked. This changes execution strategy, without qualifying native Access numeric behavior.

## Progressive terminal HAVING

Eligible global and proven-key grouped queries now apply HAVING after checked EOF,
including aggregate calls absent from SELECT. Rejected groups suppress every
selected expression and aggregate operation. Operand-bearing selected aggregates
use budgeted retained-row replay only after acceptance; Count(*)-only selections
avoid those rows, including the 100,001-input control under an 8 KiB query budget.
TOP counts accepted groups while preserving later accepted groups' eager work.
Twenty-three new controls and 531 regressions pass with strict query/native/CLI
linting, minimal query features and formatting. See [semantics and limits](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md#terminal-having-and-deferred-selected-operands)
and [verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-having-2026-10-25.json).
The [original native/CAB replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_HAVING.md) passes all 96
commands, comparing 336 successful rows and 696 cells plus six exact earlier
error-prefix rows. Fifteen immutable and thirty-four revision-source hashes were
independently checked. These engineering checks do not establish native Access
execution compatibility.

## High-offset Memo and OLE cursor reliability

Synthetic sparse sources now check external Memo/OLE payloads near the 2 GiB
boundary, nonadjacent chains, compressed Unicode and exact binary bytes in four
priority profiles. Failed later payloads discard the entire pending batch and
close continuation; pruned fields visit no payload pages. Five new tests cover
44 profile/subcases, alongside thirty existing table-page regressions and strict
engine linting. No production defect was exposed. See [scope and checkpoints](access/storage/NATIVE_HIGH_OFFSET_PAYLOADS.md);
this is synthetic geometry evidence, separate from native large-file qualification.

## Progressive static named and derived sources

Eligible row-local named/derived SELECT chains now feed a single physical cursor
without a complete intermediate table cache. Retained values preserve raw UTF-16,
Error values, declarations and comparison policies; each stage evaluates its
selected expressions eagerly and applies its own unordered TOP boundary. Outer
row, global/grouped aggregate and flat UNION ALL consumers retain their current
limits and checked EOF behavior. Inner stateful shapes and schema discovery still
refuse before scans. The CLI supports eligible explicit saved queries, external
targets and recomputed-column views with `--stream`; stored paths never open files.
Forty new controls and 498 regressions pass, with strict query/native/CLI linting
and the minimal query feature check. See [scope](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-derived-2026-10-25.json).
The [original native/CAB replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_DERIVED.md) also passes all
96 commands, comparing 420 rows and 1,410 cells. Fourteen immutable and thirty-one
revision-source hashes were independently rechecked. These checks do not
establish native Access execution compatibility.

## Progressive integral grouping

Eligible Boolean/integral/NULL GROUP BY keys now retain encounter-ordered groups
and current Count/Sum/Avg/Min/Max states through native cursors. Paired binding
metadata proves key carriers; completed key values and global policy cohorts feed
final expressions without inventing input rows. Checked EOF precedes group output,
and String extrema keep their explicit candidate budgets. The generated 100,003-row
case reduces to seventeen modeled groups; native controls exceed snapshot
retention and retain EOF/error guarantees. Thirty new tests and 429 regressions
pass with strict query/native/CLI linting, minimal query features and formatting.
See [scope](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md#progressive-grouped-aggregates) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-grouped-2026-10-25.json).
The [original native/CAB replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_GROUPED.md) also passes all
96 commands, comparing 1,374 rows and 5,364 cells across six unchanged inputs.
Thirteen immutable and twenty-five revision-source hashes were independently
rechecked. Native Access grouping qualification remains separate.

## Bounded integral join directories

Whole bare equality joins between the same proven Boolean/integral carriers now
index right-row candidates, retaining full input validation, duplicate encounter
order, outer NULL extension and original SQL comparison. Unexpected actual keys
fall back for the whole operation before output; resource failures remain errors.
The 1,100-row native/CLI controls fit default query work, while 12,000-key query
controls retain explicit finite budgets. Nineteen new controls and 123 regressions
pass with strict linting, minimal query features and formatting. See
[scope](query/QUERY_EQUIJOINS.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-directory-joins-2026-10-25.json).
An [original six-input replay](testing/DIRECTORY_JOINS.md) passes 76 commands,
comparing 51,848 rows and 105,896 cells. Old default-work refusals and new successes
are pinned separately; sixteen immutable and 37 revision-source hashes were
independently rechecked.
A [local whole-CLI benchmark](testing/DIRECTORY_JOIN_BENCHMARK.md) retains all 28
samples: these 1,100-row joins improve from 0.87–1.01 seconds to about 15 milliseconds
with equal explicit allowances and exact results. This does not qualify release
or arbitrary-workload performance.

## Larger read-only deployment packages

Qualified ACCDC inputs can now complete extraction into host-owned seekable
storage under cumulative budgets, without a whole cabinet/database Vec. The CLI
keeps existing small captures and creates an unnamed temporary file only for
larger qualified packages; failed extraction publishes no database. Inspect,
tables and ordinary rows now accept explicit native byte allowances. Fifteen
new controls and 41 regressions pass with strict Access/CLI linting and formatting.
Encryption rewrite limits and signature verification remain separate. See
[scope](access/containers/ACCDC_SPOOLED_READS.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-accdc-spooled-2026-10-25.json).
The [original large deployment replay](testing/LARGE_DEPLOYMENT.md) passes 58
controls on two 77 MiB ACE 16 databases and their stored/MSZIP packages, including
exact selected Memo digests and complete 1,100-row streams. Twelve immutable and
fourteen revision-source hashes were independently rechecked.

## Explicit widening and Hiragana

StrConv conversion 36 now applies the existing widening kernel before Hiragana
under exact explicit LCID 1041. Other previously unsupported combinations remain
refused. This is a documented engineering composition; native Access ordering
remains unqualified. Five new controls and 46 regressions pass across expressions,
queries and CLI, with strict linting and minimal expression compilation. See
[scope](expressions/text/STRCONV.md#explicit-wide-then-hiragana-composition) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-wide-hiragana-2026-10-25.json).
A separate [composition replay](testing/WIDE_HIRAGANA_COMPOSITION.md) passes
230 commands, including 616 successful cells and 24 intended refusals. Five
immutable and fourteen revision-source hashes were independently rechecked.

## Progressive global MIN and MAX

Explicit streaming queries now admit global Min/Max alongside Count/Sum/Avg,
using the existing retained-value and comparison rules. Resolver-dependent String
candidates wait for the complete policy cohort at checked EOF; raw String and
Error consumers retain their ordinary semantics. This avoids complete native
snapshots, while retained candidates remain independently budgeted. Twenty-three
new controls and 315 regressions pass across query, native and CLI targets with
strict Clippy and minimal query features. See [scope](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-extrema-2026-10-25.json).
An [original native replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_EXTREMA.md) also passes 364
controls across four profiles, comparing 396 rows and 1,584 cells. Eleven
immutable inputs and sixteen revision-source pins were independently rehashed.
Native Access comparison remains separate.

## Exact template XML names

Template XML now validates NCName/QName spellings against the exact XML 1.0
Fifth Edition ranges before namespace lookup or Access field-name escape decoding.
Valid middle-dot/combining continuations and supplementary starts work; invalid
Unicode-category approximations and malformed qualified names refuse. SQL/native
name rules remain separate. Seven new controls and 59 template regressions pass
with strict Access Clippy and formatting. See [scope](access/containers/ACCESS_TEMPLATE_DATA.md)
and [verification](testing/results/read-query-template-xml-names-2026-10-25.json).

StrConv now accepts explicit LCID 1041 through complete string-codec/locale APIs,
using the maintained Shift_JIS implementation with exact Unicode encode round
trips. Raw byte ranges, Binary decoding and caller-owned budgets retain existing
rules; single-byte Chr/Asc policies remain separate. Twelve new controls and

features and formatting. This is the explicit WHATWG-based engineering profile,
with documented Windows/mapping differences. See
[scope](expressions/text/JAPANESE_STRING_ENCODING.md) and

All five immutable and thirteen revision-source pins were independently rehashed;

Qualified ACCDT List Definition Choice fields now expose their actual stored
Text with resolved XSD agreement. Explicit nontext storage overrides remain

Checked same-table calculated expressions now compose as explicitly selected
named query views through the normal query runtime. Natural carriers, retained
String cells, paired metadata and provider policies cross filters, joins, groups,
sets and domain retrieval without casting to stored ResultType. Original tables
and stale caches retain their separate routes. CLI `--recomputed-column` selects
ordered view fields; every selected expression remains eager before outer filters.
Twenty-one new controls and 89 regressions pass with strict native/CLI Clippy,
formatting and dependency checks. See [scope](access/calculations/RECOMPUTED_CALCULATION_VIEWS.md)
and [verification](testing/results/read-query-recomputed-views-2026-10-25.json).

Access formula qualification remains separate.

## Local named template schema types

ACCDT table schemas now resolve bounded local named XSD simple restrictions,
including forward references and inherited/narrowed String/Binary/Decimal facets.
All declarations preflight before records, including unused invalid types; exact
XML names, cycle checks and independent type/depth limits remain explicit.
Existing value codecs and List Definition agreement retain authority. Eight new

## Explicit linked-table streaming

`query run --stream --link ALIAS PATH` now routes eligible scalar queries through

inert; selected fields, EOF and cumulative budgets retain existing checks, without
publishing complete snapshot caches. CLI controls also cover encrypted targets,

68 regressions pass with strict native/CLI Clippy. See
[streaming scope](cli/STREAMING_QUERIES.md#explicit-linked-tables) and

## Strict UTF-16 template XML

ACCDT control/object/table XML now accepts BOM-qualified UTF-16LE/BE alongside
UTF-8 through strict bounded decoding. Declaration mismatches, invalid surrogate
pairs and malformed units fail explicitly. Metadata-only inline schema discovery
stops before the data suffix, including an immediately malformed suffix; complete
row reads still validate it. Ten new controls and 39 regressions pass with strict
Access Clippy. Package names and original bytes remain unchanged. See
[template scope](access/containers/ACCESS_TEMPLATES.md) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-template-utf16-2026-10-25.json).

Proven uniform Boolean/integral/NULL tuples now use a metered fingerprint

preserve first encounter order. Unsupported descriptors keep the original path;
an unexpected runtime carrier disables the directory and scans all retained
representatives. Twelve-thousand-row GROUP/DISTINCT controls fit finite work
allowances without raising defaults. Eighteen new controls and 205 regressions
pass with strict query Clippy and formatting. See [scope](query/keys/EXACT_QUERY_KEYS.md)

Proven bare same-carrier integral equality now rejects join pairs before copying

A 1,100-row CLI self-join matches independent SQLite results within a 10,000-row

Explicit progressive queries now support global Sum/Avg alongside Count, prior

Concurrent states have independent scratch charges, and operand/finalization

## Progressive stored calculation reads

Explicit `query run --stream --stored-calculations` now reads qualified cached
scalar results through the existing native stored-value cursor. Formulas remain
inert and caches may be stale. Selected values retain their existing storage
validation; ordinary-only and zero-column projections prune cached payloads.
No scan fills a complete snapshot cache. Nine native and three CLI controls plus
65 related regressions pass with strict Clippy and formatting. See
[cached streams](cli/STREAMING_QUERIES.md#explicit-stored-calculations) and
[verification](testing/results/read-query-progressive-stored-calculations-2026-10-25.json).

## Declared mixed-plus result types

Known String/numeric `+` operations now expose their guaranteed successful result
under the explicit declared-arithmetic profile. Scalar String with Variant numeric
produces Text metadata, allowing UNION to apply the same result conversion as an
explicit String operation. Variant String/numeric uses existing numeric carrier
guarantees; Date, unknown declarations and default mixed-plus metadata retain
conservative behavior. Five new tests and 151 regressions pass with strict query
Clippy. See [descriptor scope](expressions/numeric/DECLARED_ARITHMETIC.md#mixed-plus-result-descriptors)
and [verification](testing/results/read-query-declared-addition-types-2026-10-25.json).

## Progressive Count operands

Explicit progressive global counts now support `Count(expr)` alongside `Count(*)`.
Each written occurrence evaluates its operand once per qualifying row through the
existing Count nullness kernel; completed counters are borrowed only during final
projection after checked EOF. NULL is excluded without forcing raw String values
through Unicode publication. Source snapshots and partial caches are not retained.
Operand failures occur during scanning, so competing errors can differ from
buffered aggregate-major evaluation order; final scalar expressions still run
after EOF. A scoped batch passes 169 query/native/CLI tests, including 23 new
controls, with strict Clippy and formatting. See
[progressive counts](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md#global-count) and the
[verification record](testing/results/read-query-progressive-count-operands-2026-10-25.json).

## Progressive exact global counts

Explicit progressive execution now handles direct-table global Count(*) queries
without retaining a complete input snapshot. Checked counters use actual qualifying
rows, and final expressions/aliases publish only after successful EOF. Flat UNION
ALL can mix count and row arms under existing promotion and cumulative controls.
The focused batch passes 138 query/native/CLI tests and strict Clippy. A generated
100,001-row input completes within an 8 KiB query allocation allowance; native
four-profile tests exceed snapshot retention caps without filling a complete cache.
See [count scope](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md#global-count) and
[verification record](testing/results/read-query-progressive-count-2026-10-25.json).
An [original four-profile CLI replay](testing/PROGRESSIVE_COUNTS.md) also passes
132 getter-modeled controls, with ten unchanged immutable pins and eleven scoped
compiled-archive hashes verified separately. That replay covers Count(*) only;
Count(expr) has the separate focused verification above. Other aggregates and
native execution qualification remain separate.

## Grouped and progressive projection aliases

Earlier explicit aliases now also compose through grouped results and explicit
progressive direct-table/UNION ALL execution. Ordered group validation prevents
ungrouped capture; streaming retains partial-row values, cumulative budgets and
full EOF checks after TOP. Immutable supplied CurrentUser context is reusable
without callbacks. Sixteen new tests and 164 related controls pass with strict

and [verification record](testing/results/read-query-projection-alias-execution-2026-10-25.json).
Crosstab dependencies and native alias qualification remain separate work.

Single-Decimal native indexes now support exact equality and NULL selections in

The explicit declared profile now retains guaranteed successful Byte/Integer/Long,

## Progressive UNION ALL

Explicit streaming now accepts flat UNION ALL chains of admitted direct-table
SELECT arms. One runtime and cumulative budgets span every arm, with ordinary
profile-specific UNION result conversion before strict scalar publication.
All arm schemas and structures preflight before output; each cursor reaches EOF
before the next starts. Per-arm TOP still evaluates omitted rows. Typed sink errors
and late failures stop later arms; the CLI preserves only completed TSV batches.

The composed slice passes 68 focused tests: 23 progressive query, nine independent
type/schema controls, seventeen native-adapter and nineteen CLI tests. Query,
Access and CLI scoped strict Clippy, formatting and the final CLI build pass.
See [the execution contract](query/PROGRESSIVE_QUERIES.md#progressive-union-all) and
[verification record](testing/results/read-query-progressive-union-2026-10-25.json).
This expands explicit streaming; distinct sets, sorts, groups, joins and named
sources remain buffered. Native Access and shared-file qualification stay separate.

## Declared Scalar String/Variant predicates

The explicit declared profile now compares a known Scalar String with a known
Variant through the existing metered CStr service. For example, `'02'=CVar(2)`
is False and `'10'<CVar(2)` is True under invariant formatting and ordinal
collation. Conversion runs once before provider resolution; actual String cells
retain their policies and raw representation. Converted numbers do not acquire
unrelated Text field authority. Unknown categories fail only when they can
change the comparison branch. Default predicates, both-Variant ordering,
Scalar numeric/Variant String conversion and strict relational keys remain
separate. See [the declared contract](expressions/numeric/DECLARED_ARITHMETIC.md#scalar-string-compared-with-variant).

The focused batch passes 143 unique Rust tests: five expression tests, 118 query

expression checking, normal CLI building, formatting and dependency checks pass.

## Explicit host-bound external query sources

The read-only query library now routes existing SELECT/FROM IN syntax through
`Source::external_source`. Exact database/connection selectors capture immutable
caller-issued binding keys during metadata-only preparation; execution revalidates
those keys before scanning root or target records. Actual target schemas,
policies, hints, optimized projections and aligned collection callbacks retain
source ownership. Each SELECT retains its lexical owner; explicit IN selects its direct table
namespace, and named definitions and domain targets retain their definition owner. Successful discovery stages retain
binding revisions to reject reuse after remapping. External named targets now use scoped identity and discovery. See [the contract](query/EXTERNAL_QUERY_SOURCES.md).

Fourteen external-source controls and 96 focused regression tests pass, including
named crosstabs, runtime domains, collection members and arithmetic-profile result
typing. The new arithmetic control checks derived/named UNION results under both
preparation and execution profiles. Strict query library/new-test Clippy and
formatting pass. This is explicit host-source engineering behavior; broader P0
semantics and Access qualification
remain unfinished.

## External IN after JOIN conditions

The SQL adapter now distinguishes parenthesized membership predicates from
external database tokens after JOIN ON expressions. Unparenthesized INNER,
LEFT and RIGHT joins preserve their ON condition and FROM selector; ON may
also contain its own IN/NOT IN list or subquery. External source syntax now
requires FROM, so malformed source-free membership does not become a database
selector. Existing formatting retains owned source/connection strings without
opening them. See [the parser contract](query/SQL_PARSER.md#access-grammar-and-formatting).

All 65 SQL library tests pass, including four new boundary/round-trip/refusal
tests and existing generated/limit controls. Strict SQL library/test Clippy passes.
This is syntax evidence, not native Access execution qualification.

## Composed query typing across arithmetic profiles

Query execution now applies the explicit mixed Decimal division rule without
changing materialized arithmetic. Bound slots and read/crosstab plans retain
separate materialized and declared result descriptions. Prepared public metadata
is conservative across modes; returned metadata and static UNION conversions use
the active runtime profile. This preserves the previous default Decimal conversion
of sibling UNION arms while admitting declared Double results through nested,
named, selector, aggregate, scalar-subquery and crosstab composition.

The [result-type contract](query/QUERY_RESULT_TYPES.md#runtime-profile-sensitive-division)

boxed crosstab read plans use checked preparation allowances. Numeric fixed-heading
folding also uses the captured declared rule, retaining eager errors before scans.

Ninety-one focused query tests pass against the final source, alongside strict
scoped query Clippy. Thirty-six CLI regression tests cover arithmetic policies,
declaration flags, cached calculations, stored text orders and linked native
sources. Normal CLI build, standalone no-default query checking, formatting,
dependency boundaries and 41 policy-script tests pass. Native Access qualification
and broader read/query/backend acceptance remain unfinished.

The explicit declared/agreement arithmetic APIs now select Double for Decimal

Decimal zero. Materialized arithmetic remains Decimal-first, while genuine
Decimal quotients continue using the existing rust_decimal path.

Stored-history discovery now accepts the ordinary Unicode-compression bit on a
qualified visible current Memo. Previously normal scalar reads succeeded while
its supported history disappeared from collection metadata. The current value
uses its existing decoder; hidden markers, template/flat field flags, mapping
and complete child membership checks retain their existing requirements.
Unknown/calculated visible flags remain refused.

The focused engine/adapter batch passes 19 tests, including five new compression
controls for metadata-only binding, aligned members, complete-cache reuse,
late orphan refusal, unsupported flags, budgets and cancellation. Strict scoped
Clippy and workspace formatting pass. See
[stored-history contracts](access/collections/STORED_HISTORY_QUERIES.md#stored-record-contract).

The [independent compressed-Memo replay](testing/COMPRESSED_MEMO_HISTORIES.md)
passes 198 controls across fresh ACE 2007/2016/2019 files, comparing declarations,
current values and stored-history queries under ordinal and database policies.
All 26 pinned hashes match. Native Access SQL, history freshness/mutation and
compressed child/template variants remain unqualified.

## Retained String numeric renderer consistency

The public retained-value evaluator now publishes valid String ranges through
the existing checked Text conversion before Str/Hex/Oct rendering. Previously
these APIs rejected the representation that ordinary bound queries already
handled. Explicit number formats, half-even integral conversion, strict Unicode
publication, eager failures and cumulative controls remain active. This closes
an API inconsistency, not a new normal-query wrong answer or complete promotion.

The focused batch passes 16 expression/query tests, including three new kernel
controls and two new bound-query parity controls. Strict scoped Clippy passes.
See [numeric rendering](expressions/numeric/NUMERIC_TEXT.md#retained-string-numeric-rendering).

## Pure text calls in native validation rules

Native field/table constraint audits now admit statically Text/NULL `Len` and
explicit binary `StrComp(..., 0)` under existing scope and resource checks.
Numeric/date formatting, locale calls and unresolved NULL results remain
unsupported. Existing Jet 4 Int32 plans and ACE 16 engineering batches evaluate
the admitted rules against complete candidates; invalid candidates fail before
publication. No physical mutation carrier or normal ACE save path is added.

The focused combined batch passes 18 integration tests, including valid/invalid
candidate checks, eager errors, empty-table preflight, UTF-16 lengths and binary
ordering. Workspace formatting passes; scoped rule units and strict Clippy also
pass. See [native validation rules](access/schema/NATIVE_CONSTRAINTS.md#bounded-validation-expressions).

The [independent text-call replay](testing/VALIDATION_TEXT_CALLS.md) passes
204 controls and 618 stored getter cells across ACE 2016/2019; all 19 pinned
hashes match. Fresh original ACE/Jet 4 validation inputs also pass the existing
12-check coverage replay without modification. Native Access equivalence and
broader validation/write qualification remain separate.

## Read-only Boolean foreign-key membership

Native constraint inspection now checks exact stored Boolean foreign keys,
including mixed nullable integer and Decimal tuples. False is a present key,
not an all-NULL exemption. Strict paired types and the existing parent unique
index requirement remain in force. Public read coverage is separate from an
internal explicit mutation-carrier allowlist, so successful Boolean membership
does not enable fixed, batch or cascade edits. An otherwise writable Jet 4 control
isolates this guard by changing only enforcement to NotEnforced.

The final combined constraint/mutation batch passes 65 integration tests, with
three focused key unit tests and strict scoped Clippy also passing. Workspace
formatting passes. See [stored Boolean relationships](access/schema/NATIVE_CONSTRAINTS.md#stored-boolean-relationship-membership).
This is the physical stored-key profile, not native Access insertion qualification.

The original [Boolean relationship replay](testing/BOOLEAN_RELATIONSHIPS.md)
passes 78 controls and 67,340 getter/index cells. Each clean ACE 2016/2019 input
has 10 tables, six enforced relationships and four confirmed node/leaf roots.
Fourteen disposable corrupt copies and two original NULL-input orphan files
correctly fail explicit audit without stdout; normal stored reading remains
available. All 27 pinned input/source/reference/executable hashes match. The
standalone minimal ACE build also passes.

## Explicit calculated-field preview in the CLI

`query preview-calculation --database PATH TABLE COLUMN` exposes the existing
restricted row-local library preview with a separate Recomputed result. It uses
ordinary dependencies, native password handling, independent resource controls
and fully buffered table/TSV output. It never enables cached-value queries, widens
formula admission, coerces to the stored declaration or saves the database.
Ten new CLI tests and two cached-query regressions pass, including encrypted
inputs, stale/corrupt caches, eager late failures and final transport limits.
Strict scoped Clippy and the CLI build pass. See
[calculation previews](access/calculations/CALCULATION_PREVIEWS.md).

The independent [CLI preview replay](testing/CALCULATION_PREVIEW_REPLAY.md) passes
44 controls and 1,018 modeled cells. Of these cells, 1,010 differ from stored
caches; ordinary NULL inputs, empty tables, unsupported declarations and corrupt
unselected caches remain separate controls. All 26 pinned hashes match after replay.
Native formula behavior and freshness remain unqualified.

## Consolidated offline read/query regression batch

The all-feature query suite passes 1,041 tests across 190 targets, including doc
tests, after the grouping/extrema, Decimal totals, selector-schema and dynamic
ordering/discovery fixes. Existing metadata controls now use genuinely dynamic
conditions where they intend unknown branch selection; retained UTF-16 observation
and strict final publication remain separately checked. Focused strict Clippy and
workspace formatting checks pass. No Windows or live Access comparison is implied.

A fresh [advanced-field evolution corpus](testing/ADVANCED_FIELD_EVOLUTION.md)
passes 60 independent getter/query controls and 18,584 returned-cell comparisons
across ACE 2016/2019 inputs. It retains untouched historical rows, relocated records,
deleted parents and changed collections alongside cached calculations. All 21
pinned source/helper/input/JAR/executable hashes match after replay. Existing reader
code handles this workload without a production change. Larger Memo projections
use explicitly larger work pools; default byte/row/output limits remain unchanged.

A freshly rebuilt immutable CLI additionally passes 197 independent replay
controls: 92 cached-value, 60 advanced-evolution and 45 mixed-scalar-history checks.
The latter compare 19,902 retained rows per ACE 16, ACE 2007 and Jet 4 file against

unchanged. The minimal query build passes; normal incremental builds remain enabled.
The [closeout record](testing/results/read-query-closeout-2026-10-24.json) retains

These checks strengthen the published stable/offline profile. They do not complete
all Partial expression contracts, calculated freshness, native text precedence,
coherent live reads or native Access compatibility acceptance.

## Numeric aggregate schemas across selector alternatives

SUM/AVG now retain a common successful output carrier when different IIf,
Choose or Switch input families feed the same accumulator result family.
Unknown or incompatible outcomes stay Dynamic; no runtime conversion or scan is
introduced. Forty-eight focused regressions, including 800 metadata cases and
1,600 executions, pass with strict scoped Clippy. This is an implementation
carrier guarantee, not native Access subtype qualification. See
[aggregate output descriptions](query/aggregates/AGGREGATE_OUTPUT_TYPES.md).

## Explicit cached calculation queries

`query run --stored-calculations --database PATH` now explicitly queries qualified
stored results through a metadata-only native source and the existing read-only
executor. Ordinary sources retain their prior eligibility. A stored projection
cursor shares normal traversal, EOF, terminal failure and cumulative controls;
pruned ordinary projections do not decode caches. Required indexes refuse cached
selections before traversal; automatic selection declines that path. Cached
provenance is exposed separately and recomputation remains distinct. See
[the query contract](access/calculations/CACHED_CALCULATION_QUERIES.md).

Five adapter, eight preview, three engine cursor and two CLI tests pass with strict
scoped Clippy. Independent stored-getter replay passes 92 controls over unchanged
Decimal/Memo fixtures and a fixed executable. This is explicit cached querying,
not freshness, formula execution or native Access query qualification.

## Wider Decimal SUM

Decimal SUM/DSum now share the existing exact fixed total with means when narrow
folds would lose precision or overflow. Final fitting/half-even conversion occurs
once; ordinary lossless folds retain their representation and non-Decimal prefix
rules remain explicit. Twenty-one focused sum/mean regressions, strict Clippy and
125 independent Fraction-model results plus five refusals pass. See
[Decimal sums](query/aggregates/DECIMAL_SUMS.md). This is the engineering numerical contract;
native Access precision and wider Variant promotion remain unqualified.

## Final-policy extrema

Min/Max now retain uncertain String candidates until the complete runtime text
policy is known, fixing a reproduced wrong-answer and unused-default-comparer
failure. Numeric/Error and stable-policy paths retain one selected cell. Six
focused regressions and the 98-test collation/domain/Error batch pass, with
once-only evaluation, singleton raw Strings, NULL provenance, cancellation and
allocation controls. See [extrema](query/aggregates/EXPRESSION_AGGREGATES.md).

This fixes the current provider contract; native Access mixed-policy precedence
remains unqualified.

## GROUP BY policy completion before partitioning

With an explicit field resolver, grouping now evaluates keys once, retains bounded
keyed rows and merges each complete key column's runtime policies before deciding
membership. Late contributors can therefore merge or separate earlier neutral
keys correctly, including across tuple partitions. Filtered-out rows do not
contribute. Global-only grouping retains incremental storage. The feature now
owns its implementation in `execution/grouping.rs`; see
[runtime policies](query/RUNTIME_TEXT_POLICIES.md).

The focused grouping/crosstab/named batch passes 133 tests, with eight targeted
regressions and strict Clippy also passing. Metadata-only binding, no rescans,
explicit overrides, eager failures, cumulative header allocations, cancellation
and named output provenance remain intact. Native mixed-policy precedence remains
unqualified; this fixes the existing explicit provider model.

## Fixed-point statistical spread

Var/VarP/StDev/StDevP now translate all-fixed numeric groups exactly before
binary64 rounding. Adjacent large LongLong, Currency and Decimal values therefore
retain nonzero spread. Mixed floating groups and explicit CDbl inputs retain their
previous conversion lane. Existing BigInt handles only bounded wide alignment;
normal offsets use i128 and stack formatting. The additional retained offset
buffer is charged explicitly. See [statistics](query/aggregates/STATISTICAL_AGGREGATES.md).

Forty focused tests and strict scoped Clippy pass. Independent Fraction replay
passes 404 result controls across 101 SQL queries against one unchanged executable.
Tests retain once-only evaluation, NULL/type/Error behavior, narrow/wide scratch
controls, cancellation and the old rounded-input result through explicit CDbl.
This is the current default numerical profile, not qualified native ACE precision
or complete Variant promotion.

## Dynamic crosstab heading policy completion

Dynamic pivots with unresolved Default provenance and an explicit resolver now
retain validated pre-WHERE candidates until the final accumulated policy is
known. This preserves both distinctions lost by an initially coarser comparer
and equivalences introduced by a later field policy. Final heading deduplication,
ordering and buckets share that policy, with no extra scan or pivot evaluation.
The final schema ceiling remains independent of bounded candidate retention;
other crosstab paths retain incremental admission. See
[runtime text policies](query/RUNTIME_TEXT_POLICIES.md).

The focused crosstab/named/collation batch passes 120 tests with strict Clippy.
Regressions cover both policy directions, filtered-out contributors, absent default
comparers, first spelling, named cache reuse, 257 candidates collapsing to one
heading, final-width refusal, quotas and cancellation. These enforce the explicit
provider model without establishing native Access policy precedence.

## Cached Long Text calculation reads

Explicit cached calculation inspection and row browsing now resolve observed
ACE 16-family Memo storage before validating its calculation wrapper and decoding
Text. Inline, single-row and chained caches share the existing bounded Memo
reader and independent encoded/decoded ceilings. NULL, empty and Unicode values
remain exact; malformed late caches suppress buffered publication. Ordinary
query eligibility and recomputed previews remain separate. See
[the cached Memo contract](access/calculations/CACHED_MEMO_CALCULATIONS.md).

Five new engine tests, nine cached-carrier regressions, four ordinary Memo tests
and eight adapter preview tests pass with scoped Clippy and formatting.
Independent replay passes 86 controls over unchanged fresh ACE 2016/2019 files,
including 28 cached cells, authored compression/BOM probes and corruption copies.
This qualifies the independent storage profile, not native Access recalculation,
freshness or all calculated-Memo declarations.

## Literal-selected result descriptors

Metadata-only preparation now preserves the successful selected carrier and
Text/Decimal constraints for literal-controlled IIf/Choose results. Switch merges
only reachable result alternatives and retains a no-match NULL possibility when
needed. Unknown controls remain conservative. Every branch still binds and runs
eagerly; Variant categories, text-policy lineage and runtime errors are unchanged.
See [selector metadata](expressions/CONDITIONAL_FUNCTIONS.md#literal-selection-and-result-metadata).

Sixty-one focused integration tests pass with strict scoped Clippy, formatting
and minimal-feature checks. Coverage includes literal/unknown descriptors,
nullable choices, derived/grouped/empty results, Single-rounded indexes, raw
String observers, dead-branch binding errors and unused clock activation. This
improves successful-result metadata, not complete native mixed-type promotion.

## Cached calculated Decimal reads

Explicit stored-calculation inspection and cached row browsing now admit the
observed ACE 16-family Numeric wrapper. A checked decoder preserves exact signed
coefficients and effective scale separately from raw column precision/scale
metadata. Unknown geometry, headers, signs and unrepresentable values refuse
without partial publication. Inert declarations and row-local recomputed previews
remain distinct; ordinary queries still reject calculated fields. See
[the cached Decimal contract](access/calculations/CACHED_DECIMAL_CALCULATIONS.md).

Five new and eight existing engine integration tests, two decoder unit tests and
seven adapter preview tests pass with scoped Clippy. Independent getter/CLI replay
passes 82 controls across fresh unchanged ACE 2016/2019 inputs, including cached
rows, empty declarations and late corruptions. This is stored-result evidence,
not native expression evaluation, freshness or Microsoft Access qualification.

## DISTINCT sort-key policy retention

DISTINCT/DISTINCTROW now retain runtime text-policy contributors from already
computed ORDER BY keys before discarding duplicates. Previously a duplicate could
carry the only nondefault policy, leaving survivors to sort under the wrong
comparer and changing TOP results. The fix preserves evaluated keys without
reevaluating expressions or changing mixed-policy precedence. See
[runtime policies](query/RUNTIME_TEXT_POLICIES.md).

The focused collation, DISTINCTROW and projected-sort batch passes 84 tests.
Three new regressions include duplicate encounter orders, reverse sorting, TOP
percent/ties, explicit overrides, fresh function policies, metadata-only binding,
eager failure, quota refusal and every observed cancellation checkpoint.
This establishes the existing explicit provider contract, not native Access
mixed-field precedence.

## Native cursors at the read-source boundary

Original sparse-source controls now read actual synthetic table rows from the
last two pages of a virtual 2 GiB file under small cumulative budgets. Complete,
scalar-projected and zero-width cursors retain exact values and one-read-per-page
continuation. Final-page failures close the cursor without publishing a suffix;
complete materialization refuses failed or corrupt tails. Out-of-range usage-map
bits and over-ceiling source lengths fail before data reads. See
[high-offset read evidence](access/storage/NATIVE_READ_FAILURES.md#cursor-reads-at-the-2-gib-source-boundary).

Five focused tests cover 32 scenarios across Jet 4 and ACE 2007/2016/2019 layouts.
These controls exercise native traversal, rather than header recognition alone;
they do not qualify native large-file creation, throughput or live coherence.

## Captured decimal integer literal typing

The explicit `--declared-arithmetic` query profile now captures decimal integer
literal carriers during preparation: Integer, Long and then Double by unsigned
magnitude. Plain preparation and default execution retain their existing profile.
Literal carriers and provenance propagate through named/domain discovery and
closed crosstab headings; exact integral scan hints remain conservative. A typed
literal is one plan leaf, preserving the existing structural depth allowance.
See [the literal contract](expressions/numeric/DECLARED_ARITHMETIC.md#captured-decimal-integer-literals).

Focused numeric, retrieval, crosstab, declaration and date tests pass 109 controls,
with five binding-budget/cancellation tests and two closed-heading/runtime
negation parity tests also passing. The independent literal and declaration
replays pass 197 and 5,550 controls against one unchanged CLI copy. Scoped Clippy,
formatting and diff checks pass. This is an opt-in engineering policy; native
Access literal subtypes and complete Variant promotion remain unqualified.

`query run --text-locale` now composes optional ICU text comparison/search with

SQL StrReverse now retains reversed complete UTF-16 units across raw-aware

Private index-column storage now uses ArrayVec under the existing ten-key native
ceiling. Public slices, field ordering, raw flags and qualification remain intact.
The owning NativeIndex vector includes inline capacity in its allocation charge;

qualification. Direct SmallVec and memchr experiments remain development-only; production InStrB
retains its existing work/cancellation contract.

## Explicit row-local calculated-expression previews

The engine exposes inert qualified calculated-field declarations without reading
records. The Access adapter can separately prepare and execute restricted pure
same-table arithmetic, concatenation and NULL tests over ordinary fields. A

eligibility is unchanged. See [calculation previews](access/calculations/CALCULATION_PREVIEWS.md).

Six integration tests and one syntax/dependency test pass, including stale/NULL
and corrupt unselected caches, metadata-only preparation, inert SQL-like Text,

engine cached-calculation tests and scoped adapter Clippy pass. Broader functions,

qualification remain unfinished; no database is updated.

The query binder now accepts DECIMAL(p,s)/NUMERIC(p,s) using the existing checked

Four query tests cover all admitted precision/scale pairs and scope conflicts;

`query run --native-text-bytes` now selects decoded native Memo bytes through the

`--collections` now exposes actual resolved hidden-field Memo history Text and

Named crosstabs now derive fixed schemas for policy-independent constant IIf,

## Retained logical operands and Empty admission

Not and all six binary logical operators now admit explicit host Empty as
Integer zero under the existing effective-type rules. Raw String operands remain

hiding a later eager expression failure. NULL/zero peers cannot suppress required

logical/coercion/raw-arithmetic query tests pass. The independent runner passes

engineering evidence; native Access, broader P0 promotion and remaining backend
acceptance are unfinished.

The original exact-rational boundary runner passes 23,460 controls through both
CLI evaluators over 2,890 operand pairs and 11,560 binary operations. Every
supported scale pair, signed 96-bit ceiling/midpoint neighbors, cancellation and

Direct native Short Text equality can now use automatic or explicit matching
indexes when the actual database-policy resolver and source agree. Full residual

budgets, source order and complete-cache isolation remain enforced. AND,
inequalities, Memo and wider policies remain outside this new hint profile. See

and production writes are unfinished.

`query run --comparison-bytes/--comparison-steps` now controls the existing

2007/2016/2019 inputs, including both General versions. Read-only Jackcess getters

TOP/First/Last, row limits, later complete scans, eager errors and chosen-root
corruption failures on disposable copies. Original hashes are unchanged. Full

## Count over lossless String expressions

Count/DCount now use the shared lossless operand service to observe String
nullness without Unicode publication. Previously Count failed on an unpaired
UTF-16 unit or odd-byte range before counting it. Expression evaluation, Error
counting, unsupported Empty/Missing cells, checked Int64 totals, NULL omission,
filters, empty groups and domain criteria retain their existing contracts.
Invalid constructors and CStr(NULL) still fail; no failed expression becomes an
omitted NULL row. Other aggregate consumers and raw relational storage remain
unchanged. See [contracts and Microsoft query reference](query/aggregates/EXPRESSION_AGGREGATES.md#counting-lossless-string-expressions).

every observed checkpoint. Query all-target all-feature and focused CLI Clippy,
minimal query compilation, formatting, Python compilation and diff checks pass.
Independent runners pass 774 new raw String cardinality/refusal controls and
1,026 existing encounter/NULL/Error controls, using source-free inputs only.

No dependency, stored carrier, native decoder or writer changed. Full expression,
engine/workspace suites, native Windows Access and benchmarks were not run for
this chunk. Wider aggregate/Variant and read/query acceptance remain unfinished.

## Lossless String admission in numeric arithmetic

Subtraction, multiplication, division, integer division, Mod and power now admit
raw String intermediates before NULL propagation. Previously an unpaired UTF-16
surrogate beside NULL failed Unicode decoding prematurely. Both operands still
evaluate eagerly, unsupported families and Error/Missing retain their refusals,
and non-NULL Strings strictly publish Text before existing numeric conversion.
Original-type Empty division and declaration-aware Date/integral dispatch remain
in their owning services. Shared string operand handling now lives in its own
execution feature module, retaining grouped runtime policies and declarations.
See [numeric String contracts](expressions/numeric/ARITHMETIC_TEXT.md).

The NULL regression was observed failing before the fix. Verification passes:

## Grouped policy retention in composed string operands

A regression could lose accumulated group-key text policy when a composed key
was reused inside another ampersand/plus or CVar string operand. Re-evaluating
the neutral representative returned a Default-policy value even though later
group rows had contributed a field policy. Scalar cells already performed the
required enrichment. Both paths now share a feature-local result-policy walk,
using the existing metered structural identity and correlated scope matching.
Values still evaluate normally; this adds no value cache, provider discovery or
native mixed-policy precedence rule. Fresh text-function defaults and explicit
global overrides remain unchanged. See [runtime contracts](query/RUNTIME_TEXT_POLICIES.md).

RGB now uses the formal Integer argument width for red, green and blue before

Checked, promoted, declaration-aware and contextual arithmetic now share explicit

and [contextual rules](expressions/numeric/ARITHMETIC_TEXT.md).

## Shared OS locks for CLI native reads

Raw/encrypted CLI native inputs now own the existing read-only SharedFile guard;
CAB/template probes and captures and encryption-copy sources use the same lock.
Cooperating exclusive writers cause immediate payload-free LockBusy before
interpretation or output; shared readers coexist. Raw guards remain owned through
query/cursor use and release on every return path. Owned package captures may
release their input guards after capture. Existing offline UPDATE copies already
used this mechanism. No new dependency, retry, lock upgrade, native Access lock
protocol or immutable whole-file capture is introduced. Stable/offline inputs
remain required. See [coordination limits](access/writes/NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS.md#cli-read-coordination).

browsing, deployment, distribution-name, encryption and inspection tests pass.
Source bytes and fresh-output absence are checked. CLI all-target/all-feature
Clippy, build, formatting and diff checks pass. Full workspace/backend suites,
benchmarks and Windows/native Access coordination comparisons were not repeated.


## Absolute I/O seek-position validation

The shared absolute read/write helpers now reject a seek callback that reports a
different position from the requested offset. InvalidSeekPosition carries no
payload and maps to native Malformed. Failure occurs before the read/write
callback, even for empty buffers; existing seek work, byte-charge ownership and
cancellation/host error behavior are retained. This protects custom sources that
report the mismatch; it cannot detect falsely reported positions or provide a
concurrent-file snapshot. Native shared-file coordination remains unfinished.

keeps its own bound and can require TSV. The flags do not apply to eval, parse,

LVAL rows, with a separate 1 MiB decoded UTF-8 Memo ceiling. Attachment decoding
admits 1 MiB files in both stored and zlib modes, a 4 KiB header and 2 MiB encoded
storage. Cycle scanning charges its bounded work; Memo decoding charges logical
input passes and retains before/after cancellation checks. All caller budgets,
query Text limits, CLI output limits, source/image envelopes and write gates
remain explicit. [Larger payloads](access/storage/LARGE_PAYLOADS.md) records the boundaries.

## Runtime domain-result text provenance

Internal query cells now carry expression values with host-issued text policies.
DLookup/DFirst/DLast/DMin/DMax retain the actually bound result policy through
selectors, aliases, derived/correlated rows, groups, sets, sort/TOP ties, pivots and
operation-local named-crosstab materialization. Public stored/expression values and
source contracts retain their existing shape; preparation still performs no domain
scans or provider calls. Static domain metadata stays Default without discarding
runtime provenance.

Sort/set-key contributors merge before comparison. Group/heading representatives
retain policies from matching discarded cells, so a neutral literal cannot hide
later policy conflicts. Grouped output and correlated expressions use the existing
structural identity rules through a shared metered plan service. Fixed headings
are rechecked when a runtime pivot policy becomes known. Raw projection and global
comparison overrides retain their prior behavior; fresh text functions keep the
existing provisional Default policy.
